title: Sign in
description: Access your private server inventory on this installation.
notes: Hosted and self-hosted use the same identity flow; this is a simulated form, not a provider choice.
Expired session clears cached account/target state; sign-out returns here. Unauthorized is not an empty inventory.
Labels, associated validation errors and keyboard focus precede submission.

title: Your servers
description: Private inventory · changes apply without redeploying.
notes: Only owned inventory from the management API is eligible; guessing another user's ID cannot grant access.
Add/edit via server-form, verification via host-trust; deletion requires exact target/revision review and invalidates sessions/caches.
Empty: Add your first server. Loading: skeleton. Unauthorized: sign in. Disconnect retains inventory but disables live operations.
Revision conflict: reload/compare; never overwrite stale revision automatically. Search and internal scroll preserve mobile access.

title: Add or edit server
description: Provide connection metadata and a new write-only credential.
notes: Production fields: name, hostname, port (1–65535), SSH username, environment, key provisioning or credential replacement; edit binds server revision.
New secret value is never echoed or populated from saved storage. Clear after successful provisioning and on account change; exclude from logs, analytics and hydration.
Deletion confirmation repeats target and revision; failure-before-submit leaves inventory unchanged. Conflict offers compare/reload. Rotation invalidates relevant connection state.
Mobile fields stack with error association; submit focuses first invalid input.

title: Verify host identity
description: An observed host key has not yet been independently verified.
notes: Show algorithm/fingerprint/source and observation time. Independently compare using a trusted channel, then record explicit verification.
Changed key blocks connection and requires renewed verification; never offer accept-all or label first observation trusted.
Unavailable observation differs from mismatch. Unauthorized users cannot enroll another owner's server.

title: Agent connection
description: One installation endpoint; authorization scopes access to your owned servers.
notes: Copy public endpoint, follow separate authorization, inspect granted scopes and expiry, revoke owned grant. No URL token/SSH secrets.
Revocation/expiry disables subsequent calls; URL possession never grants access. Unknown client compatibility remains an identity-owner decision.
Disconnected agent status is distinct from dashboard session expiry. Self-hosted install uses its own domain/database/identity boundary.
